headline: Water for Injection by membrane
lead: Our membrane systems produce Water for Injection (WFI) at ambient temperature from double-pass reverse osmosis (RO), electrodeionization (EDI) and ultrafiltration (UF), with no plant steam for generation.

body: USP has long allowed WFI from any process equivalent or superior to distillation. The European Pharmacopoeia did not. In April 2017 the revised Ph. Eur. monograph 0169 began to allow WFI by reverse osmosis, single or double pass, coupled with other suitable techniques such as EDI, ultrafiltration or nanofiltration.

The quality limits did not change. Membrane WFI must meet the same conductivity, TOC and endotoxin limits as distilled WFI. What changed is the evidence inspectors expect: a contamination control strategy, as EU GMP Annex 1 describes, that shows how the system controls microbes and endotoxins without the heat of distillation.

blocks.caption: Two RO passes remove dissolved solids, organics and most microbes. EDI polishes conductivity. The final ultrafiltration membrane retains endotoxins and bacteria. The skid is hot water sanitized on a fixed cycle, and online TOC and conductivity confirm quality before water reaches storage.

items.q: Will Health Canada and the FDA accept membrane WFI?
items.a: USP has allowed it for decades and both agencies inspect against it. The burden is on your data: a sound design, a documented contamination control strategy and a performance qualification that covers seasonal feed water changes.

items.q: How long should performance qualification run?
items.a: Common practice is a three-phase PQ over about a year, so seasonal variation in feed water is captured. We write the sampling plan with your validation team.

items.q: Can we convert an existing PW system to membrane WFI?
items.a: Often, if the existing RO and EDI are in good condition. We assess it and add a final barrier, sanitization and instrumentation as needed.
